name: How language and meaning flow through the model
gist: Models transform words into abstract concepts and back. These papers track how semantic information moves through layers, how syntax gets separated from meaning, and where translations happen.
explain: Language models process text token by token — one chunk at a time — and each token is first converted into a numerical vector called an embedding (a list of numbers that represents the token in a way the model can work with). As the token flows through layers, this vector is transformed, mixed with information from surrounding tokens, and gradually becomes something richer. By the final layers, the same token's representation has absorbed context: 'bank' in 'river bank' is represented differently from 'bank' in 'the bank is closed.' This research asks: where and how does this transformation happen? At what layer does the model separate the surface form (spelling, word order) from the meaning?

The core challenge is that language has layers of structure: sound, syntax (grammar), and semantics (meaning). A model has to build all three and coordinate them. Do early layers extract syntax while later layers add meaning? Or does it happen all at once? Some research uses probing classifiers — attaching a small auxiliary model to read out hidden states and asking, 'if I measure at this layer, can I predict the part of speech?' Others track how specific token positions influence each other through attention. By building this map, researchers understand how language gets parsed and reassembled inside the model, which matters for spotting errors or biases introduced during that processing.

papers.title: A geometric relation of the error introduced by sampling a language model's output distribution to its internal state
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that token space geometry directly reflects internal problem representations, with transformations clustering by board region and piece importance.

papers.title: Expand Neurons, Not Parameters
papers.contribution: Widening networks while maintaining constant non-zero parameter count consistently increases accuracy on Boolean tasks, CLIP classifiers, and multilayer networks, matching modern accelerator strengths.

papers.title: From Associations to Activations: Comparing Behavioral and Hidden-State Semantic Geometry in LLMs
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that forced-choice behavior predicts hidden-state similarity better than free association, showing behavioral-only measurements capture recoverable information about internal semantic geometry.

papers.title: Negative Pre-activations Differentiate Syntax
papers.contribution: Sign-specific ablation of negative Wasserstein neurons increases perplexity and degrades grammatical performance, yielding a double dissociation between syntax and non-grammatical capabilities.

papers.title: Paradigm Shift of GNN Explainer from Label Space to Prototypical Representation Space
papers.contribution: Enables more expressive explanation of graph structures by leveraging vectorized graph representations and addresses entanglement and distributional discrepancy between input and explanation subgraphs.

papers.title: Reading Images Like Texts: Sequential Image Understanding in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: The analysis reveals two-stage visual processing from attribute recognition to semantic disambiguation, enabling efficiency improvements and spatial reasoning enhancements via RoPE scaling.

papers.title: Rethinking LLM-as-a-Judge: Representation-as-a-Judge with Small Language Models via Semantic Capacity Asymmetry
papers.contribution: INSPECTOR substantially outperforms prompting-based small LMs and closely approximates full LLM judges on reasoning benchmarks while offering efficiency, reliability, and interpretability.

papers.title: SK2Decompile: LLM-based Two-Phase Binary Decompilation from Skeleton to Skin
papers.contribution: Achieves 21.6% re-executability gain over GPT-4-mini on HumanEval and 29.4% R2I improvement over Idioms on GitHub2025.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Information-Decomposition Analysis of Large Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Analysis reveals two task regimes (synergy-driven vs. knowledge-driven) and two opposing family-level strategies (fusion-centric vs. language-centric), identifying visual instruction tuning as key to learning fusion.

papers.title: Abstraction Induces the Brain Alignment of Language and Speech Models
papers.contribution: A layer's intrinsic dimension strongly predicts fMRI/ECoG signal prediction; the relation arises during pretraining; finetuning causally increases both intrinsic dimension and semantic content, showing alignment derives from rich meaning abstraction.

papers.title: Boosting for Predictive Sufficiency
papers.contribution: The framework provides theoretical grounding for boosting's success in OOD generalization; validation through synthetic and real-world experiments shows boosting achieves robust performance by identifying environments and maximizing outcome association.

papers.title: Bridging Functional and Representational Similarity via Usable Information
papers.contribution: Provides unified theoretical and empirical synthesis linking functional, representational similarity and reconstruction via task-granularity hierarchy.

papers.title: Concept Heterogeneity-aware Representation Steering
papers.contribution: CHaRS yields more effective behavioral control than global steering through input-dependent cluster-level shifts via barycentric projection.

papers.title: Confidence is Not Universal: Task-Dependent Calibration and Emergent Behavior in LLMs
papers.contribution: Shows universal confidence calibration fails across task families but within-family transfer works; decompositional approach restores cross-family generalization.

papers.title: ConvexBench: Can LLMs Recognize Convex Functions?
papers.contribution: Achieves F1=1.0 at depth 100 versus 0.2 for standard approaches by addressing parsing failure and lazy reasoning failure modes.

papers.title: Decoupling Dynamical Richness from Representation Learning: Towards Practical Measurement
papers.contribution: The metric is empirically more stable than alternatives and captures lazy-to-rich transitions like grokking without relying on accuracy measurements.

papers.title: Embedding Trust: Semantic Isotropy Predicts Nonfactuality in Long-Form Text Generation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that higher semantic isotropy reliably signals lower factual consistency across samples and consistently outperforms existing aggregate trust signals using only a handful of samples.

papers.title: Exploratory Causal Inference in SAEnce
papers.contribution: The method achieves the first successful unsupervised causal effect identification on real-world scientific trials.

papers.title: Exploring Interpretability for Visual Prompt Tuning with Cross-layer Concepts
papers.contribution: Achieves superior interpretability and performance over visual prompt tuning and existing interpretable methods on fine-grained classification benchmarks with different network depth explanations.

papers.title: Formal Concept Lattices are Good Semantic Scaffolds for Concept-Based Learning
papers.contribution: Produces more interpretable embeddings supporting effective interventions with hierarchically structured concept representations.

papers.title: How Do Language Models Speak Languages? A Case Study on Unintended Code-Switching
papers.contribution: Reduces code-switching rate by 20.8% through fine-tuning the identified language sub-circuit with minimal parameter updates (~0.019% of all neurons), offering mechanistic insights into multilingual LLM generation.

papers.title: Inferring the Invisible: Neuro-Symbolic Rule Discovery for Missing Value Imputation
papers.contribution: On synthetic and real-world datasets, the framework effectively imputes missing values while uncovering meaningful, human-interpretable rules that govern system dynamics.

papers.title: LLMs Lean on Priors, Not Programming Language Semantics
papers.contribution: Across 11 frontier LLMs, strong final-state accuracy (up to 90%) drops sharply by 40-60 percentage points under semantic mutations, with even the best achieving only 35% long-horizon conditioning accuracy.

papers.title: Large Vision-Language Models Get Lost in Attention
papers.contribution: Shows that replacing learned attention weights with predefined values (e.g., Gaussian noise) yields comparable or superior performance, exposing severe misallocation in current attention mechanisms.

papers.title: LinguaMap: Which Layers of LLMs Speak Your Language and How to Tune Them?
papers.contribution: Selective fine-tuning achieves over 98% language consistency across six languages while fine-tuning only 3-5% of parameters, matching full-scope fine-tuning with fewer resources.

papers.title: Multilingual Routing in Mixture-of-Experts
papers.contribution: Reveals language-specific routing in early/late layers, cross-lingual alignment in middle layers, 1-2% consistent multilingual gains via inference-time steering.

papers.title: Patronus: Interpretable Diffusion Models with Prototypes
papers.contribution: Interpretable diffusion models enable shortcut detection and semantic emergence tracing while maintaining strong generative performance.

papers.title: Precise and Interpretable Editing of Code Knowledge in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves neuron-level mechanistic interpretability with precise correspondence between edited neurons and specific code knowledge; systematically evaluates KE methods.

papers.title: Real-Time Visual Attribution Streaming in Thinking Model
papers.contribution: Achieves faithfulness comparable to exhaustive causal methods while enabling live attribution streaming as the model reasons across five benchmarks and four thinking models.

papers.title: ReasonEdit: Editing Vision--Language Models using Human Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art editing performance across four VLMs on rationale-based visual QA, demonstrating that human reasoning greatly improves edit generalization.

papers.title: Rethinking Code Complexity Through the Lens of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that LM-CC exhibits strong partial correlations with LLM performance, and semantics-preserving reductions in LM-CC lead to improved downstream task performance.

papers.title: See the Emotion: A Facial Emoji Proxy Modeling for EEG Emotion Recognition
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on EAV and MMER benchmarks while generating semantically faithful facial animations providing transparent windows into neural emotional evolution.

papers.title: Semantic Regexes: Auto-Interpreting LLM Features with a Structured Language
papers.contribution: Semantic regexes match the accuracy of natural language descriptions while being more concise and consistent, enabling quantification of feature complexity and user studies showing improved mental models.

papers.title: Should I Have Expressed a Different Intent? Counterfactual Generation for LLM-Based Autonomous Control
papers.contribution: Provides formal guarantees that counterfactual outcome sets contain the true outcome with high probability; demonstrates advantages over naive re-execution baselines.

papers.title: Sparse CLIP: Co-Optimizing Interpretability and Performance in Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: Sparse CLIP achieves superior interpretability and downstream performance compared to SAEs while preserving multimodal capabilities and enabling interpretable vision-language steering.

papers.title: Syntax vs. Semantics: How Transformers Learn Deep Dependencies
papers.contribution: Shows Chain-of-Thought bypasses suppression regime; topology-aligned contrastive objective achieves 2x larger improvement than cross-entropy on variable binding.

papers.title: The CoT Encyclopedia: Analyzing, Predicting, and Controlling how a Reasoning Model will Think
papers.contribution: Produces more interpretable analyses, enables prediction of model reasoning strategy, and improves problem-solving and safety benchmarks.

papers.title: The Expert Strikes Back: Interpreting Mixture-of-Experts Language Models at Expert Level
papers.contribution: Resolves debate on specialization showing experts function as fine-grained task experts in linguistic operations and semantic tasks, MoEs are inherently interpretable at expert level.

papers.title: The Truth Lies Somewhere in the Middle (of the Generated Tokens)
papers.contribution: Pooling embeddings produces more informative representations than single tokens, indicating semantic information is distributed across generated tokens rather than localized.

papers.title: TimeSeg: An Information-Theoretic Segment-Wise Explainer for Time-Series Predictions
papers.contribution: Produces more coherent and human-understandable segment-wise explanations capturing holistic temporal patterns.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Modality Interaction in Multimodal Language Models via Partial Information Decomposition
papers.contribution: PID identifies that reasoning tasks show high synergy while knowledge tasks rely more on language alone, and reveals a sensory synergy bottleneck in omni-modal models dominated by visual information.

papers.title: Uncovering Semantic Selectivity of Latent Groups in Higher Visual Cortex with Mutual Information-Guided Diffusion
papers.contribution: Identifies neural latent groups with clear semantic selectivity to diverse visual features including object pose, inter-category transformations, and other attributes in IT cortex.

papers.title: Visual Persuasion: What Influences Decisions of Vision-Language Models?
papers.contribution: Optimized edits significantly shift VLM choice probabilities, revealing consistent visual themes driving selection and supporting proactive auditing.
